output.answer_1: Let (i, j) name a grid point: i steps right and j steps up-right from the lower-left corner. Draw the outline through (0,0), (2,0), (1,1), (0,2), and back to (0,0). Put the trapezoid with vertices (0,0), (2,0), (1,1), and (0,1); put the triangle on its short side from (0,1) to (1,1), with its third point at (0,2).
output.answer_2: Using the same grid-point directions, draw the outline through (0,2), (2,2), (2,1), (3,0), (1,0), (1,1), and back to (0,2). Draw the shared edge of the two trapezoids from (1,1) to (2,1).
output.answer_3: Using the same grid-point directions, draw the outline through (0,1), (0,2), (1,2), (2,1), (2,0), (1,0), and back to (0,1). The two trapezoids share the long edge from (0,1) to (2,1). This hexagon is different from the one in Part B.
output.answer_4: Using the same grid-point directions, draw the outline through (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (2,0), (2,1), (1,2), (0,2), and back to (0,1). The trapezoid has vertices (0,1), (2,1), (1,2), and (0,2). Put one triangle below each unit section of its long side from (0,1) to (2,1): their third points are (1,0) and (2,0), respectively.

**Evaluating lattice construction**

I'm considering how to use lattice coordinate construction. I want to represent an equilateral triangular lattice using cells, specifically unit triangles. So, I'm exploring defining a trapezoid made of three equilateral triangles and looking at its vertices in lattice coordinates. 

The trapezoid vertices would be (0,0), (2,0), and (1,1) with specific edge directions. I wonder about the area determination for this shape and how it all fits together in this coordinate system.
